items.name: TV console
items.imageNote: Ownership is confirmed. The exact console photo is not yet reliably identified; no surrounding store furniture is assumed to be yours.
items.dimensionNote: Measure the complete unit, usable TV opening and any doors or drawers.
items.verdict: Reuse before shopping for another TV stand.
items.placement: Use an uninterrupted solid wall in the family TV hall, with a clear route to the entry and stairs. Check screen size and cable access.
items.color: Finish identification pending. Keep a sound existing finish and repeat one wood tone in small accessories.
items.next: Send or identify the console photo and measure width × depth × height and any TV opening.

items.name: Dark desk currently holding the monitors
items.imageNote: Furniture-only AI reference based on your private lower-office photo #027. It is a visual illustration, not an exact product drawing or measurement.
items.dimensionNote: Actual width, depth, return length and height are not recorded. The 61-inch dimensions on the pale L-desk listing do not belong to this desk.
items.verdict: Use the desk you own; skip a second office desk.
items.placement: Keep the current desk in the lower creative office first. Measure its footprint, return, chair space and heater clearances before buying replacement furniture or extra screens.
items.color: Dark brown and black can anchor the room. Keep other storage light and use a few restrained plants.
items.next: Measure the existing desk and screen widths. Check its top and frame ratings before selecting monitor mounts.
items.source: You confirmed the dark desk holding the monitors in gallery #027 as the purchased desk.

items.name: Narrow oak glass-door bookcase
items.imageNote: The narrow middle cabinet is the purchased bookcase. Surrounding store furniture is not counted as owned.
items.dimensionNote: No reliable cabinet dimensions in the supplied photo. Measure its widest crown, deepest base and full height.
items.verdict: Keep the oak finish, touch up wear and reuse it for books.
items.placement: Prayer-room solid-wall corner near the curtain. Fit and anchoring must be checked on site; keep a gap from seating, curtain fabric and heater clearance zones.
items.color: Honey oak matches the existing floor. Warm ivory, restrained sage and russet accents can coordinate without repainting it.
items.next: Record cabinet and corner measurements. Inspect glass, supports and hinges; anchor the sound frame to a suitable wall fixing.
items.source: Gallery image #019 and your purchase clarification.

items.name: Orange / russet chaise sofa
items.imageNote: Shared store photo. This sofa has not been confirmed as purchased.
items.dimensionNote: Photo tag matches Bob’s Bettie Russet Chofa: 86 W × 64 maximum D × 33 H. Manufacturer also describes an 86 × 36 straight-sofa configuration with the included cushion. Verify the exact unit and components with the seller.
items.verdict: Color works; tape out the chaise before reserving it.
items.placement: You asked to try this in the second hall. The 86-inch width is within your 84–96-inch shopping target, but the 64-inch chaise goes well beyond the earlier 36–42-inch sofa-body depth target. Try the straight configuration first if the prayer floor becomes crowded.
items.color: Russet complements honey oak and white. Use quiet cream or sage textiles; do not buy a second strong accent sofa to match it.
items.next: Confirm the total delivered price, exact model, configuration, condition and room route. No purchase recommendation until the floor trial works.
items.source: Your store photograph and the manufacturer’s dimensions, checked 7 November 2026.

items.name: White cabinet pieces / pantry reuse
items.imageNote: Earlier shared cabinet photo. Confirm whether these are the same TV-console parts or a separate set before counting another item.
items.dimensionNote: Component dimensions and panel thickness are missing. Weight alone does not establish load capacity.
items.verdict: Measure and inspect before buying a replacement pantry.
items.placement: Potential dry-storage material for the former white-fridge bay. Retain the existing orientation where possible; a horizontal console is not automatically safe when turned upright or stacked.
items.color: White can tie into existing kitchen trim. Finish exposed edges and keep damaged particleboard away from moisture.
items.next: Photograph the laid-out panels with dimensions and label each piece. Decide one primary use; the same console cannot serve both the hall and pantry.
items.source: Pantry Cabinet Design: you said the heavy cabinets were acquired and dismantled. Photo identity needs matching to the confirmed TV console.

items.name: Light 61-inch L desk — reference only
items.imageNote: Shared listing reference, not the desk you confirmed as purchased.
items.dimensionNote: Photo labels show two 61-inch outer runs; arms are 23½ and 20 inches deep. The 61 × 61 figure is the L-shaped outer envelope, not a solid square desktop. Height is unrecorded.
items.verdict: Skip a second desk while the dark workstation already meets the need.

notes.title: Former white-fridge bay
notes.detail: Use 66 inches as the conservative height until measured. Removing the louvered upper cupboard could allow roughly 96 inches overall; check what it conceals first. Include doors, handles, trim and installation space.

notes.title: Hall / mini-hall sofa target
notes.detail: This is a preferred furniture envelope, not the complete room size. A chaise has its own deeper projection. Check actual uninterrupted wall length and circulation.

notes.title: Hall coffee-table target
notes.detail: Optional purchase. Your later second-hall request omitted the coffee table, so keep the prayer floor open there.

notes.title: Dining table target
notes.detail: Tape out the smaller end first. A 72 × 36 table with a 36-inch clearance band on all sides occupies a 144 × 108-inch planning envelope; chair and passage needs may require more.

notes.title: Mini-hall table alternative
notes.detail: A different-size table idea, not an instruction to buy an extra table. Choose one everyday dining setup after checking what remains in the home.

notes.title: Large bedroom for children
notes.detail: Three separate movable beds remain the direction. Keep the left-side closet and bathroom access clear. Hot-water baseboards run along most walls; their required clearance still needs confirming.

priorities.label: Use first
priorities.title: Place the three purchases
priorities.text: Assign one home to the console, desk and bookcase. Clean and repair sound furniture; add suitable restraints and cable management before buying duplicate storage.

priorities.label: Measure next
priorities.title: Resolve the large footprints
priorities.text: Measure the sofa wall and chaise projection, bookcase corner, desk corner, pantry pieces and children’s bed layout. Tape the outlines on the floor and walk the routes.

priorities.label: Consider later
priorities.title: Buy a missing function
priorities.text: Prioritize actual sleeping needs, one necessary seating setup and measured closet supplies. Buy a coffee table, rug or dining replacement only after the main furniture is placed.

priorities.label: Skip for now
priorities.title: Avoid duplicate furniture
priorities.text: No second TV console, office desk or display bookcase. Pause full matching sets, extra benches and large restoration projects without a specific measured place to use them.
